title: Product weight gap bound
statement:
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be finite sets, and let $a,c:\alpha\to\bbr$ and $b,d:\beta\to\bbr$. Suppose $b(y)\ge 0$ for every $y$, $c(x)\ge 0$ for every $x$, and $\sum_y b(y)=\sum_x c(x)=1$. Then
\[
\sum_{(x,y)\in\alpha\times\beta}\abs{a(x)b(y)-c(x)d(y)}\leq \sum_{x\in\alpha}\abs{a(x)-c(x)}+\sum_{y\in\beta}\abs{b(y)-d(y)}.
\]
replaced:
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be finite types, and let $a, c : \alpha \to \bbr$ and
$b, d : \beta \to \bbr$ be real-valued weight functions. Suppose $b$ and $c$ are
nonnegative and each sums to one, i.e.\ $b(y) \ge 0$ for all $y$, $c(x) \ge 0$ for all
$x$, $\sum_{y \in \beta} b(y) = 1$ and $\sum_{x \in \alpha} c(x) = 1$. Then the $\ell^1$
gap between the two product weight functions is at most the sum of the marginal $\ell^1$
gaps:
\[
\sum_{(x,y) \in \alpha \times \beta} \abs{a(x)\,b(y) - c(x)\,d(y)}
\;\le\; \sum_{x \in \alpha} \abs{a(x) - c(x)} + \sum_{y \in \beta} \abs{b(y) - d(y)}.
\]
